background_notes.fact: In a complex vector space of finite dimension n, every complex basis has exactly n elements. Hence an integer basis of M that is also a complex basis of V can be reindexed by Fin(ell+1) here.

For nonnegative λ, ell is the corresponding natural number, so λ+1 corresponds to ell+1.

background_notes.justification: Relative to n coordinates, finite linear elimination bounds the size of any independent family by n and forces any spanning family to have at least n elements. An infinite independent family would contain n+1 independent vectors, which is impossible. Thus a basis has exactly n elements; reindexing this same family by Fin n preserves both its integer and complex basis properties.

background_notes.fact: A basis indexed by Fin n is a finite spanning family, so its space is finite dimensional. If n>0 over a field, its vector at index 0 is nonzero and the space is nonzero.

background_notes.fact: For integer modules M and K, each element of either tensor product is a finite sum of pure tensors. Additive balanced formulas determine maps out of these tensor products, and additive maps agreeing on all pure tensors agree everywhere. With K a field and scalar multiplication on its tensor factor, scalar compatibility on pure tensors proves K-linearity.
